Title: Bob Spence Obituary
Content:
Peacefully, after a hard-fought battle with cancer, God called Bob home to play in the "Ultimate Major Leagues", at the age of 74. Loving husband and best friend of Karen (Shaw) for 48 years. Much loved Dad to Shannon and her husband Brad Archibald. Cherished and proud Papa to Zach and Luke. Very dear uncle to Dave and Sherry Robins and their children Joey and Justin. Will be greatly missed by brother-in-law George Robins and best friends Wayne and Lorraine Powell, as well as family in Nova Scotia and England, and many friends in Hamilton and throughout Southern Ontario. Predeceased by his beloved sister Bonnie Robins, and parents Erwin and Evelyn Spence. Bob loved golfing and playing baseball with the Hamilton Oldtimers Baseball Organization, cheering on his Ti Cats, Leafs, Raptors, and Blue Jays, but most of all, being with friends and family. Bob and Karen were blessed to attend The South Gate Presbyterian Church and appreciated all the support from their friends there. Special thanks to our amazing Oncologist Dr. Hotte. For over 40 years, Bob enjoyed a rewarding career in journalism, with the majority of time spent with Thomson Newspapers and the Information and Privacy Commission of Ontario. Flowers gratefully declined. If desired, donations to the Canadian Cancer Society would be greatly appreciated. We would like to thank all of our friends and family who were with us throughout Bob's cancer journey. Your love, support and your continual prayers will never be forgotten. Most of all, we thank God, who walked this road with us, and has now carried Bob to victory.
 
A Celebration of Life service will be held on Saturday, October 16, at 11 a.m., at Gateway Church, 15 Haldimand Rd 66, Caledonia, (905) 765-5407. Due to Covid restrictions and gathering limits, registration is required. Register at:
https://gatewaycaledonia.churchcenter.com/registrations/events/1027540
 
*The service will also be live streamed for those unable to attend in person.

Title: HOBO 55 RULES
Content:
HOBO 55 RULES                                                                                                                          05-JUN-2025

1. A batter is safe at first when an outfielder touches the ball. He can be thrown out if he rounds first with the intention of running to second.

2. Each pitcher is limited to a maximum of nine outs and those outs must be consecutive. For example, a pitcher cannot pitch the first inning, play another position (or sit out) the second inning, and then return to the mound in the third inning.

3. Games are to be nine innings long. For regular season games, no new inning can start after two hours thirty minutes. This curfew does not apply to playoff games.

4. If the score is tied after nine innings in a playoff game, the international tie breaking rule will be applied (i.e. each half-inning will start with the last out of the previous inning being placed at second base).

5. A maximum of five runs is allowed per team per inning except:

     - On an over the fence home run.

     - In an “open inning” (i.e. the last inning, as declared by the umpire).

6. A runner on 3rd base cannot score on a pitch not caught cleanly by the catcher.

7. A pinch runner can only advance to 2nd or 3rd on a pitch not caught cleanly by the catcher. and touches the ground after contact with the catcher.

8. Metal cleats cannot be worn while pitching or batting.

9. A catcher who reaches base safely base must be pinch run for when there are two out. Such a pinch runner can attempt to steal.

10. All pinch runners must be the last out, unless that player is injured (in which case the pinch runner must be the previous out). The spirit of this rule is to prevent a team from using a faster runner in a pinch runner situation.

11. Stealing is not allowed if the offensive team is ahead by three or more runs.

12. Bats must be made of wood. Metal bats and composite bats are not allowed.

13. Unlimited defensive substitutions are allowed (except for pitchers).

14. Unlimited defensive shifts are allowed.

Title: HOW TO SCORE
Content:
A scorer will give an error to a fielder if the play could have been made with "ordinary effort," meaning that a player of average skill could have caught or fielded the ball given the field and weather conditions. 

 

Ways of Making an Out

 
Result Abbreviation Example Result Example Abbreviation
Strikeout swinging K Swing and a miss K
Strikeout looking Backwards K Called third strike Backwards K
Groundout The position number of the player who fielded it followed by the number of the player who caught it Shortstop fields it and throws to the First Baseman 6-3
Flyout The number of the player who caught it Center Fielder catches it 8
Lineout L followed by the number of the player who caught it 2nd Baseman catches it L4
Unassisted Play The number of the player who made the play followed by U Pitcher fields it and tags the runner (or the base) 1U
Caught Foul Ball F followed by the number of the player who caught it Third Baseman catches it in foul territory F5
Sacrifice Fly SF followed by the number of the player who caught it Left Fielder catches it SF7
Sacrifice Bunt SB followed by the number of the player who fielded it followed by the number of the player who caught it Catcher fields it and throws to the First Baseman SB2-3
Double Play:
For the runner: The number of the player who fielded it followed by the number of the player who caught it Shortstop fields it and throws it to the Second Baseman 6-4
For the batter: The same as the runner, but add in the player who catches the ball next followed by DP Shortstop fields it and throws it to the Second Baseman who throws it to the First Baseman 6-4-3 DP

 

 

Tracking Hits

 
Result Abbreviation Example Result Example Abbreviation
Single 1B
Double 2B
Triple 3B
Home Run HR
Hit By Pitch HP or HBP
Walk BB
Error E followed by the number of the player who committed the error The shortstop bobbles the ball and throws it away E6
Fielder's Choice FC With a runner on first, a grounder is hit to the second baseman who only gets the lead runner out (the fielder has made a choice not to try to get the batsman out). FC
Dropped Third Strike K

 

 

Tracking Base Running

 
Result Abbreviation Example Result Example Abbreviation
Stolen Base SB
Caught Stealing CS Thrown out by the catcher while attempting to steal CS
Picked Off PIK Picked off by the pitcher PIK

 

 

Scoring RBI's

Score an RBI for balls put in play

Score an RBI for the batter when a runner scores as the result of a safe hit, a sacrifice bunt, a sacrifice fly, an infield out, or a fielder’s choice out.

Score an RBI for a walk

Score an RBI for the batter when the bases are full and the batter is awarded first base because of a base on balls, because they are hit by a pitch, or because of interference or obstruction.

Don't score an RBI for double plays

Don’t score an RBI for the batter when a runner scores during a force double play or a reverse-force double play.

Scoring an RBI on an error

Don’t score an RBI for the batter when a run scores because of an error committed by the fielding team that would’ve completed a force double play. 

Score an RBI for the batter when there is only one out and the fielding team commits an error on a play during which a runner on third base would have scored despite the error.  Score an RBI for the batter when a fielder holds the ball or throws it to the wrong base if the runner keeps going. If the runner stops and, upon noticing the error, starts running again, the run is scored as a fielder’s choice rather than an RBI.  Score an RBI for the batter if an error is made on a play but the official scorer determines that the run would’ve scored regardless of the error.

Title: Playoff format - five-team league
Content:
Format

The playoff format will be as follows in years when the league has five teams:

QF1 = 5 @ 2

QF2 = 4 @ 3

SF1 = (loser of QF1 or loser of QF2 – which ever had the better regular season record) @ 1

SF2 = (winner of QF1) v (winner of QF2) – home team is team with better regular season record

Final = (winner of SF1) v (winner of SF2) – home team is team with better regular season record

Legend

QF = quarter-final

SF = semi-final

1 = first-place team, regular season

2 = second-place team, regular season

3 = third-place team, regular season

4 = fourth-place team, regular season

5 = fifth-place team, regular season

Honoring Four of Baseball's Pioneers:

Since the 2021 season, HOBO 55 has honored the first African Americans to play for the three big league clubs that have namesake teams in our league:

- Dodgers – number 42 – Jackie Robinson

- Cardinals – number 10 – Tom Alston

- A’s – number 23 – Bob Trice

- Tigers - number 22 - Ozzie Virgil

The right sleeve of our jerseys is adorned with the number of the corresponding player.

To see stats and biographical info relating to these players, please see the LINKS section of this web site (under the "ABOUT" menu option).
